author: KXRM
title: Schwachheim Fire near Trinidad reaches 1,000 acres - NewsBreak
text:
10 hours ago
(SOUTHERN COLORADO) — The Colorado Springs Fire Department (CSFD) is sending its Brush 3 truck and crews in response to a resource request to support efforts in fighting the Schwachheim fire just southeast of Trinidad in Las Animas County after the fire reached 1,000 acres at 0% containment as of Wednesday, April 15.
According to the Hoehne Fire Protection District, the Schwachheim Fire began on Sunday at Lake Dorothey, near the border of New Mexico, and spread quickly, jumping to 150 acres overnight and then to 450 acres within a day, despite efforts from multiple agencies, including air drops, to contain it.
Courtesy: Hoehne Fire Protection District The Colorado Incident Management Team (CIMT) took over management of the fire on Tuesday and is working closely with local and national resources. On Monday, Governor Jared Polis verbally declared the fire a disaster emergency, allowing the activation of the State Emergency Operations Plan and directing several national resources to take appropriate actions to assist with response, recovery, and mitigation efforts.
As of Wednesday, a combination of dozer line construction and retardant drops has been set up on the southwest side of the fire, holding the left flank from Lake Dorothey up to the mesa top. Helicopters are working on the east side in the drainage to keep the fire west of the East Fork of Schwachheim Creek to the mesa top.
According to CIMT, the fire has been burning in grass and brush in an old burn scar area of rugged, steep drainages, and west and southwest winds have been pushing the fire to the north and northwest.
Lake Dorothey State Wildlife Area is closed, and flight restrictions are in effect in the airspace above the fire, including a no-fly zone for drones. No evacuation orders are currently in effect, but locals are encouraged to sign up for Las Animas County, Colorado emergency alerts .
According to CSFD, the crew left to join firefighting efforts early on Wednesday morning, and their deployment could last for up to 14 days.
